text: An offer does not stay open indefinitely.
Describe the ways in which an offer can come to an end and assess whether the law in this area
is still subject to uncertainty. [25]
Describe the vitiating factors of fraudulent misrepresentation and unilateral mistake as to identity
and assess their respective merits when bringing an action. [25]
Describe the legal rules governing expectation loss and reliance loss in a claim for damages.
Assess the extent to which limitations imposed by the law restrict a claimant’s right to choose on
what basis to make a claim. [25]
Section B
Julius has to present a history lecture in London on Roman Britain. When he sets out, his car will
not start. His neighbour, Kira, agrees to his request to drive him there and back in her car. When
they return Julius says he is so grateful for her help and he will pay her £100. He does not.
After the lecture Julius meets Mia. She has published a book by Julius and is contracted to pay
him £1000. Mia explains that she cannot pay the full amount and asks if Julius would settle for
£500 plus a copy of a rare first edition book on Roman coins. He agrees.
Consider whether or not consideration will be found to make Julius’s agreements with Kira and
Mia enforceable. [25]
Ranjit is a regular paying visitor to Thrillseekers Theme Park (TTP). On this particular visit, he
breaks his arm when he is thrown from a ride because TTP has failed to properly maintain the
safety belt. The camera he is holding is damaged beyond repair.
When Ranjit seeks compensation, TTP denies liability. They highlight a clause printed on the back
of his admission ticket and displayed on a notice at the ticket office which states:
Thrillseekers Theme Park accepts no liability for any
loss or injury to visitors however this may arise.
Advise Ranjit whether he can successfully claim against TTP in Contract Law for his injury and the
loss of his camera. [25]
Nina invites her brother, Omar, to her house to watch the final of a tennis tournament being shown
on a pay-per-view sports channel. She says she will pay for the broadcast if Omar supplies some
food. He agrees but fails to bring anything to eat.
Feeling hungry, Nina visits Premium Pizza. She has seen the company’s advertisement in a
newspaper promising a free soft drink to every customer who buys a pizza. When she has paid
and received her pizza, she is told the free drink is not available because they have run out of
stock.
Advise Nina whether the agreements she has made with Omar and Premium Pizza are
enforceable. [25]
